# Test data

`invoice.pdf` (15,809 bytes) is a real-world PDF: LibreOffice 24.2
(`soffice --headless --convert-to pdf:writer_web_pdf_Export`) converted a
small HTML page set in DejaVu Sans to it. It embeds a subset of DejaVu Sans
as a TrueType font with a ToUnicode map; DejaVu fonts are under the
Bitstream Vera license with public-domain changes, which allows
redistribution. The text is made up and contains no personal data:

```text
Rechnung Nr. 2026-10
Müller & Söhne GmbH, Straße 5, 80331 München
Gesamtbetrag: 1.234,56 €
Leistung: Proﬁl-Prüfung, Größe XL
```

"Proﬁl" is written with the ligature U+FB01, which extraction normalises
to "fi".

`encrypted-user.pdf` and `encrypted-owner.pdf` (1,241 bytes each) are
one-page PDFs encrypted with the standard security handler, revision 6
(V 5, R 6, AES-256, `/CFM/AESV3`). They were generated by
`pdftest.Encrypted` at commit `fafbad2`, which was then removed so that
no password hashing or encryption code stays in the repository:

| File | User password | Owner password | Page text |
|---|---|---|---|
| `encrypted-user.pdf` | `user-secret` | `owner-secret` | `hidden words` |
| `encrypted-owner.pdf` | empty (opens without one) | `owner-secret` | `open words` |

These are test passwords, not secrets.

Every other PDF the tests use is built at test time by `../pdftest`.
